copy.approximate_caveat: This layer shows approximately where the California Department of Fish and Wildlife's 2016 aerial survey mapped kelp. Kelp beds grow, shrink and move from season to season and year to year, so this shows the kelp as it was photographed in 2016, not as it is today. CDFW mapped the kelp at 2 metres; it is drawn here generalized to about 50 metres, and patches closer together than about 50 metres are drawn as one bed.
copy.classes_verbatim: Surface kelp canopy and subsurface kelp classifications are separate.
copy.no_kelp_mapped_verbatim: An area where no kelp data are present may represent an area devoid of kelp, or may represent an area where kelp was not detected due to poor photo quality, missing photo coverage, or other issues with data collection and processing.

method.geometry: CDFW's 2-metre survey polygons, assembled into parts by containment, merged where parts lie within about 50 m of each other (a closing: grow 25 m, shrink 22.5 m), simplified at 50 m in CDFW's own metres, then projected to longitude/latitude at 5 decimal places.
method.every_part_rule: No part CDFW mapped is dropped. Every one of the survey's parts is inside, or within 50 m of, a drawn part; a part that the merge or the simplification would have lost is drawn as CDFW mapped it.
method.datum_note: The survey is NAD83 (California Teale Albers). Inverse-projected coordinates are published as WGS84 without a datum shift: the NAD83-WGS84 difference in California is on the order of a metre, fifty times smaller than the generalization.
